scope: Internal Linux one-peer JSONL/WebSocket carrier only; not activated or composed with the editor launcher or upstream Codex transport.
implemented: Private directory/device/inode and exact newly bound socket identity; never unlink an existing or substituted socket.

Ready precedes parent-supplied exact peer PID/birth/executable SHA-256. SO_PEERCRED, current-user and executable metadata/hash verify before HTTP upgrade or message delivery; no child/ancestor/title fallback.
One accepted peer, no reconnect. Parent and peer liveness/identity rechecks; nonblocking bounded buffers; 1 MiB messages, 16 KiB handshake and eight-second initial deadline.
Masked client frames, UTF-8 fragmentation, extended lengths, ping/pong and bounded close; duplicate JSON keys, binary/reserved/unmasked/malformed frames and unexpected handshake options refuse.

Normal EOF/deadline/termination retire only the original socket. Abrupt owner loss kills the carrier through setpriv parent-death signaling; the owner must verify identity and retire the remaining exact socket.

retainedFailure.cause: A cleanup SIGTERM could raise a late TimeoutError and emit an interpreter traceback. SIGTERM now exits silently with protected exact-socket cleanup; a dedicated stop test and full ingress/package rerun pass.

limits: The synthetic end-to-end wire check feeds matching account/resume frames into the existing protocol witness. It starts no real provider/task, authorizes no forwarding and claims no IDE attachment.
Final relay ownership, source-peer binding, launch/return wiring, original-account sampling and native TUI parameter compatibility remain unfinished.
No frontend, installed state, device, account, model or native-task effects. No new dependency/runtime was installed.
